summary:
Forest Pulse is an interactive satellite data-analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to monitor forest health, track vegetation indices, and detect deforestation signals. Powered by NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 (250m resolution NDVI and EVI) and NASA POWER climate archives, the platform enables users to select any forest coordinate worldwide and analyze historical satellite observations up to 2026.

By integrating an automated least-squares linear regression engine and period-over-period shift analysis, Forest Pulse quantifies canopy trends, classifies natural vegetation biomes, and generates comprehensive automated ecological reports. Crucially, it correlates vegetation health with surface temperature and precipitation metrics to distinguish climate-driven drought from direct human-induced clearing, empowering researchers and conservationists with transparent Earth-system insights to protect vulnerable ecosystems.
details:
We utilized Super Intelligence (AI) tools (such as large language models like Gemini) as a collaborative development assistant to accelerate our innovation workflow for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Specifically, AI tools were utilized in the following areas:

  • Code Architecture & Structuring: Assisting with backend routing logic (Node.js/Express) and structuring the frontend dashboard components (HTML/CSS/JavaScript).
  • Documentation & Content: Drafting and organizing the project descriptions, submission details, and presentation slide outlines.
  • Debugging & API Integration: Troubleshooting asynchronous data fetching, error handling, and parsing for NASA MODIS and NASA POWER datasets.
